newsitem.title: USA: Miami corruption case delays annual note sale.
newsitem.headline: Miami corruption case delays annual note sale.

text.p: Corruption charges against several top Miami officials delayed by at least three weeks the $15 million tax anticipation note sale that had been planned for Oct 1, an official involved in the deal said Friday.

The city commission was scheduled to approve the $15 million TAN sale at its meeting on Thursday. But the item was pulled from the agenda after the sudden resignation of finance director Manohar Surana, and after the filing of criminal charges against city officials left the finance department and the commission meeting in chaos.

The issue has been put back on the city commission agenda for Oct 10. Because the sale is by competitive bid, the city would then have to advertise the deal for at least 10 days before it could accept bids, the official said.

City Manager Cesar Odio and City Commissioner Miller Dawkins were charged Wednesday with federal crimes stemming from alleged bribes and kickbacks involving city contracts. Federal prosecutors said Surana, who resigned Aug 30, had agreed to plead guilty to unspecified charges and had worn a hidden wire to record converstions implicating Odio, Dawkins and lobbyist Jorge de Cardenas, who was also charged.
Odio subsequently resigned his post and Dawkins was suspended. The city council appointed former Dade County Manager Merrett Stierheim as acting city manager.
The city has issued tax anticipation notes annually since 1989 to manage cash flow. Its TANs are rated SP1-plus by Standard & Poor's and MIG-1 by Moody's Investors.
Officials involved in the note sale said the city would still be able to meet its payroll, but that finances would be strained until tax receipts start coming in in November.
